newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police raid sect after child dies.
newsitem.headline: French police raid sect after child dies.

text.p: French police raided the homes in southwest France of a U.S.-based sect on Monday after detaining two members whose child died from malnutrition and lack of medical care, police said.
They said an investigating magistrate was probing members of the sect, called Tabitha's Place, on suspicion of failing to assist a person in danger.

Sect members Raphael Ginoux, 36, and his German-born wife Dagmar were remanded in custody at the weekend after their 19-month-old son Raphael died last week from malnutrition and an untreated heart ailment.
They are being formally probed for failing to give the child adequate care.
Investigators said some 100 adults and 70 children live at two farms owned by the sect, in Angous and Sus near Pau. Sect members refuse outside medical care and teach their children themselves.
